SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT

〔右上角印章及手写内容〕
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
& S. B. REGISTRY
File No. N. D 4822
Special Branch-S2 / Shanghai 7-3
Date May 6, 19 33.

Subject (in full) Application for employment in the Shanghai Municipal Police
from one Samuel Lew Tee Soo ( 刘 禄 書 ).
Made by and Forwarded by [签名]

With reference to the attached application dated April 29,
1933 from one amuel Lew Tee Soo, for employment in the Municipal
Police, I forward herewith a specimen of a translation of an
extract from a communist handbill, which was made and typed by
him without assistance. Attached is also a statement containing
brief particulars of his antecedents, which was also compiled and
typed by him without help.

The applicant admits that whilst being but a recent arrival
in Shanghai, he has no connections, but feels with the experience
he has had in the past in dealing with political investigations,
it would only be a question of time in getting accustomed to
local conditions, before he would be able to establish liaisons
with persons who could supply him with information affecting
illegal organisations.

He is anxious to work in any capacity as he almost destitute,
his room rent only being covered by the amount of baggage that
he has with him at present. He states that at present he
would not worry about the salary paid him were he to secure a
position in the Municipal Police, as his main Object in life at
present is to earn enough to procure for him his daily food..

Forwarded herewith are also letters of recommendation from
the Acting Commissioner of Police, Kedah, and from the Assistant
Superintendent of Police i/c Detective Branch, Penang, which
indicate that Mr. Samuel Lew Tee Soo was an investigator of no
small ability in the above mentioned localities.

[签名]
Detective Inspector.

Officer i/c Special Branch. Not engaged - m
instructions 7/5. S.B. SBR 10/5

报告

〔右上角印章及手写内容〕
上海公共租界工部局警务处
及特别科登记处
档案编号 N. D 4822
特别科-S2 / 上海 7-3
日期 1933年5月6日。

主题（全称） 一名叫 Samuel Lew Tee Soo（刘禄书）者申请受雇于上海公共租界工部局警务处。
由 [签名] 提交并转呈

关于附件中 dated 1933年4月29日由 Samuel Lew Tee Soo 提交的受雇于工部局警务处的申请，现随函附上由他独立制作并打字的一份共产党传单节选译文稿样本。另附一份由其独立编写并打字的简要身世说明。

申请人承认，虽然他是初到上海，并无关系网，但他认为凭借过去从事政治调查的经验，适应本地情况只是时间问题，此后便能与那些能提供涉及非法组织情报的人员建立联系。

他急于以任何身份工作，因为他几乎身无分文，目前的房租仅靠变卖随身行李来支付。他表示，如果能在工部局警务处谋得职位，目前并不在意薪水多少，因为他当前的主要人生目标是赚取足以维持每日伙食的费用。

随函还附有吉打州（Kedah）代理警务处长和槟城（Penang）侦探科助理警司的推荐信，表明 Samuel Lew Tee Soo 先生在上述地区是一位能力不俗的调查员。

[签名]
侦探督察。

特别科主管警官。未参与 - 根据 5月7日指令。特别科 特别科登记处 5月10日

Statement made by Samuel Lew Tee Soo on 5.5.33

The following brief narration is the history of my life.
I was born in the year 1908 and was brought up in Burma
where I have studied both at St Aiden's S.P.G. Chinese
School, Moulmein and at Judson's Boy's High School at
Rangoon up to 9th standard.
The discontinuation of my study was due to the death of
poor father in 1924.
In 1926 I was engaged to teach both English and Chinese
at my alma-mater---- St Aiden's S.P.G. Chinese School
on a salary of Fifty Rupees.
The resignation of this post was due to the successful
application for a post of a teacher at Rangoon St Paul's
High School in which I remained as a teacher for over
a year.
The salary I drew from the school was only sixty five
Rupees.
I again left the services for an officiating interpre-
ter at Rangoon Small Causes Court for a period of six
months after which my services were dispensed with
owing to the fact that the permanent incumbent had return-
ed from leave.
After the loss of my services I was so unlucky that I
was compelled to stay at home with my mother in Rangoon
town for more than a year.
At last I came out of her house with her consent and
knowledge, and went to Singapore to seek my fortune;
but unfortunately I could not accomplish my expectation.
Having had been an unemployed at Singapore, I went to
Penang and stayed at a certain Hotel.
During my stay at Penang I applied for a clerical job
at the Detective Station, but I was selected as a special
investigator and my subordinate office was to translate
the seditious documents seized from communists.
I left the situation in the year 1932 on my own accord for
Burma.
Here I was drawing $ 100/- per mensem.
pages.zh:
Samuel Lew Tee Soo 于 1933年5月5日所作的陈述

以下简述为我的人生经历。
我生于1908年，在缅甸长大，曾在毛淡棉（Moulmein）的圣艾丹教会（S.P.G.）中文学校和仰光（Rangoon）的贾德森男子中学（Judson's Boy's High School）就读至九年级。
学业中断是因为家父于1924年去世。
1926年，我在母校——毛淡棉圣艾丹教会（S.P.G.）中文学校受聘教授英语和汉语，月薪五十卢比。
辞去该职是因为成功申请到仰光圣保罗中学（St Paul's High School）的教师职位，我在那里任教一年多。
我从学校获得的薪水仅为六十五卢比。
我再次离职，去仰光小额诉讼法院担任临时口译员，为期六个月，后因正式任职者休假归来，我的服务便被终止。
失业后，我运气不佳，被迫在仰光市区与母亲同住了一年多。
最后，在征得母亲同意并让她知晓的情况下，我离开她的家，前往新加坡谋生；但不幸的是，我未能实现期望。
在新加坡失业一段时间后，我去了槟城，住在一家旅馆里。
在槟城期间，我申请了侦探站的一名文员职位，但我被选为特别调查员，下属办公室的工作是翻译从共产党人那里缴获的煽动性文件。
1932年，我自愿离开该职位返回缅甸。
在那里，我每月薪金为100元。

pages.en:
In the same year Mr J.L. Lemerfather, the Commissioner
of Police of Kedah State in Malaya sent for me from Burma
through Mr.E.V. Fowler, Assistant Superintendent of Police
in Charge of the Detective Branch, Penang for investiga-
tion purposes.
Here my monthly pecuniary remuneration was $ 80/- and
expenses in addition.
I left him this year in the month of January for some-
where else; because I was surrounded by the communists
who tried to harm me after their important organisations
and their essential members have been raided and arrested.
The object my coming here is, on the one hand, to save
my life from being assassinated and to earn my livelihood
by attaining a situation .

（签名）
5/5/33

P.S.
My father was a Chinese whose name was Lew Nyo Yee, was
a Licensee of Country Spirit Shop in Rangoon Town.
My mother is a Burmese named Ma Aye Lay is now living
at No. 238.Eden Street , East Rangoon.
I left Penang in the middle of March for Hongkong by
Dutch steamer named "VONHOCK".
Remained a few days in hotel at Hongkong, I then came
to Shanghai by SUCHIAN steamer.
As my complexion does not resemble a Burmese, no Chinese
authority has ever abstained me from being landed.
I first put up in Kwong Thai Lay hotel at Avenue Edward VII
for a week in which I have attempted to find another
cheaper lodging house, and found the present house No.I99,
R 8, Carter Road where I have been dwelling to the present
date.

（批：Szechuan）

（签名）
pages.zh:
同年，马来亚吉打州（Kedah State）警务处长 J.L. Lemerfather 先生通过槟城侦探科主管助理警司 E.V. Fowler 先生，将我自缅甸召去从事调查工作。
在那里，我的月薪为80元，此外还有津贴。
今年一月，我因故离开他前往别处；因为在其重要组织和核心成员遭到突袭和逮捕后，共产党人试图伤害我，使我处于包围之中。
我来此的目的，一方面是为了避免被暗杀以保全性命，另一方面是为了谋得职位以维持生计。

（签名）
1933年5月5日

附言：
我的父亲是中国人，名叫 Lew Nyo Yee，是仰光市区一家乡村烈酒店的持牌经营者。
我的母亲是缅甸人，名叫 Ma Aye Lay，现居住在仰光东区伊甸街（Eden Street）238号。
我于三月中旬乘坐名为“VONHOCK”的荷兰轮船离开槟城前往香港。
在香港的旅馆停留数日后，我乘“四川”号（SUCHIAN）轮船来到上海。
由于我的肤色不像缅甸人，中国当局从未阻止我上岸。
我首先入住爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的广泰来旅馆（Kwong Thai Lay hotel）一周，期间试图寻找更便宜的住所，最终找到了现在的住处：卡德路（Carter Road）199弄8号，并居住至今。

（批注：四川）

（签名）

Specimens of translating and typing
made by Samuel Lew Tee Soo on 4-8-33.

A Notification to unemployed labourers in celebrating
of May Day.
Unemployed Labourers!
Our May day has come again!
The May Day of last year, our Shanghai labourers were due
to the bombardment of imperialist Japanese that they were
thrown greatly out of employment.
There are , at present, about four hundred thousand
unemployed workers who are begging for bread.
This year the imperialist Japanese is extending war as to
occupy the territory of Jehol in the Northern part of China.
The K.M.T. is not being able to protest against the
military action of the Japanese army, but, on the contrary,
the K. M. T. is employing every possible means to fleece
or exploit military fund from the oppressed and toiled
masses for annihilating the RED ARMY.
Therefore it is the only cause of the great deal of pitiful
masses are starving to death.
Unemployed workers!
We are now exceedingly suffering.
We can never hope to get help from the Capitalistic K.M.T.
They will only oppress us to pay the increment of taxes,
house rents and water supply fees; if we are unable to
meet such a heavy payment we would at once be compelled
to deliver up the possession of dwelling and the water
supply would at the same time be cut off;
When we beg for salvation the K.M.T. says that
we are opponents to them , we are only to be really killed
and be put in jail in any way.
They are being desirous of us to be out of job and to be
really killed by starvation.
The men who are working under capitalists are being heavily
exploited and are gradually thrown out of employment.
Now, look at the Japanese Factories, Chinese Factories and
all other large Factories that are run by capitalists have
again put the Five Day's system and Three Day's System
into execution as to throw a great number of labourers out
of employment.

Samuel Lew Tee Soo 于 1933年4月8日制作的翻译和打字样本。

庆祝五一劳动节致失业工人的通告。
失业工人们！
我们的五一节又到了！
去年的五一节，由于帝国主义日本的轰炸，我们上海的工人遭受了巨大的失业打击。
目前，约有四十万失业工人在乞求面包。
今年，帝国主义日本正在扩大战争，以占领中国北部的热河领土。
国民党无法抗议日军的军事行动，相反，国民党正利用一切可能的手段，从受压迫和劳苦的民众身上榨取或剥削军费，用于消灭红军。
因此，这就是大量可怜民众饿死的主要原因。
失业工人们！
我们现在痛苦至极。
我们绝不能指望从资本家的国民党那里得到帮助。
他们只会压迫我们缴纳增加的税款、房租和水费；如果我们无力支付如此沉重的费用，我们将立即被迫交出住房使用权，同时供水也会被切断；
当我们乞求救赎时，国民党说我们是他们的反对者，我们只会被真正地处死或以任何方式投入监狱。
他们希望我们失业，并被饥饿真正夺去生命。
在资本家手下工作的男人正受到严重剥削，并逐渐被解雇。
现在，看看日本工厂、中国工厂以及所有其他由资本家经营的大工厂，它们又重新实行五天工作制和三天工作制，以便将大量工人抛出就业岗位。

上海公共租界工部局警务处
中央及特别科登记处
编号 D H 832
日期 __ / 1 . 5 . 1933

致，
首席警务官，
警务部，
南京路，
上海。

来自，
Samuel Lew Tee Soo。
上海卡德路（Carlie Road）199弄8号。

日期 1933年4月29日于上海。

先生，
我谨恭敬地呈上以下事实，供您审阅和帮助：
我出生于缅甸，并在那里成长和教育。我现年二十五岁。我并非自吹自擂，说我不仅能读写英语和汉语，还能读写缅甸语；我也并非自我吹嘘，说除了上述国家的语言外，我能流利地说各种方言，如：普通话、粤语、福建话、克伦语（Kayinese，这是我的母语）、马来语和印度斯坦语。我曾在仰光小额诉讼法院担任临时口译员六个月，后因正式任职者

下转第1页。

pages.en:
incumbent had returned from leave. That I was
sometimes ago a teacher both in St Aiden's S. P. G.
Chinese School, Moulmein and St Paul's High School
at Rangoon, Burma. That I was in the employment
of Mr. E. V. Fowler, Assistant Superintendent of police
in charge of Detective Branch, Penang as being a
reliable man for secret investigation work. And
that after years' services, I resigned the post and went
back to Rangoon which is my birthplace.
That I was further employed by Mr. J. P. Penne-
father Evans, Commissioner of Police of Kedah
State in Malaya, who called for me from Burma
through Mr. Fowler's recommendation for arresting
and investigating the political activities held in
that State by Communist Party, where I have
effected many arrests, and raided most of their
unlawful organizations. That, after the success
of the investigation work the Commissioner of police
as well as the British Adviser to the State were very
pleased with it. But, finding that it was very disastrous
to my life as their remaining members were bearing
grudge and employing various means to harm me, a
resignation was then made with the consent and
knowledge of the Commissioner, and have come for
safety to this place where I have never been.

9- T. O. 2.
pages.zh:
休假归来，我的服务便被终止。我不久前曾在缅甸毛淡棉的圣艾丹教会（S.P.G.）中文学校和仰光的圣保罗中学担任教师。我曾受雇于槟城侦探科主管助理警司 E. V. Fowler 先生，作为一名可靠人员从事秘密调查工作。在服务多年后，我辞职回到了我的出生地仰光。
后来，我又受雇于马来亚吉打州警务处长 J. P. Pennefather Evans 先生，他是通过 Fowler 先生的推荐从缅甸将我召去，以逮捕和调查共产党在该州举行的政治活动，在那里我实施了许多逮捕，并突袭了他们大多数非法组织。调查工作成功后，警务处长以及该州的英国顾问对此非常满意。但是，鉴于其剩余成员怀恨在心并利用各种手段伤害我，这对我的生命极为危险，因此在征得警务处长同意并使其知晓的情况下，我提出了辞职，并来到这个我从未到过的地方以求安全。

下转第2页。

pages.en:
That, since I set foot in Shanghai I have all the
time been looking for a job that would probably
keep me on, but my strenuous effort has always
been in the result of no avail. That I am now in
great trouble; it is not because of my laziness,
but because of my lack of friends here to
recommend. That if I were to walk along either
forward or backward with an empty purse, it is
absolutely impossible. Therefore it is my last
attempt to come to you with this epistle
for beg of you giving a hand to rescue me
out of the distress I am experiencing. Should I
were lucky enough to be favoured with a job in
your office or with otherwise, I shall be greatly
thankful to your great kindness. In the event of
your kindness of being allowed me to have an inter-
view with you, I shall be highly pleased to call
at your office at once on production of the
documents I have got from my prior employers.
Trusting that my humble prayer will not be all in vain.
A favourable reply is earnestly expected by,
with thanks in anticipation,        I beg to remain,
                                    Sir,
〔此处转录不清〕                      yours obediently,
                                    Gus Lee 888
                                    m
pages.zh:
自从我踏足上海以来，我一直在寻找一份能让我维持下去的工作，但我艰苦的努力始终徒劳无功。我现在处境艰难；这并不是因为我的懒惰，而是因为我在这里缺乏朋友推荐。如果我囊中空空，无论是进是退，都绝对不可能。因此，这是我最后的尝试，致信给您，恳请您伸出援手，将我从现在的困境中解救出来。如果我有幸能在贵部门或其他地方获得一份工作，我将对您的大恩大德感激不尽。若您惠允与我面谈，我将非常乐意在出示前任雇主提供的文件后立即前往您的办公室拜访。
相信我这卑微的请求不会完全落空。
急切期待您的 favorable reply，
预先致谢，          我谨呈，
                                    先生，
〔此处转录不清〕                      您顺从的仆人，
                                    Gus Lee 888
                                    m
pages.guess: 本页有 1 处标注为影像不清。这类页面影像质量较差，**其余部分的转录可能包含较多推测**——模型会尽量读出残损处的文字，偶尔会猜错。引用前请对照左侧原件影像核对。
